title: Tracking debris smaller than 10 centimeters
bottleneck: Fragments under 10 cm are too small for routine radar and optical tracking yet carry enough kinetic energy at orbital velocities to destroy a satellite — and they are the most numerous debris class, growing with every collision and anti-satellite test. Operators fly blind through this population: conjunction warnings cover only tracked objects, so avoidance maneuvers cannot dodge what is not cataloged. Space-based sensors and better radar could help, but coverage, cost, and data-sharing barriers persist.
why_it_blocks: You cannot avoid or remove what you cannot see; the untracked population is the dominant collision risk for mega-constellations and crewed stations.
current_state: The US Space Surveillance Network tracks 30,000+ objects down to about 10 cm; LeoLabs and others add commercial radar. The sub-10-cm population, likely millions of objects, is estimated only statistically.
